stories.head: Israel kills Hamas Rafah brigade commander in Gaza strike
stories.say: An Israeli strike in Khan Younis has killed Samir Abu Younis, head of Hamas's Rafah brigade. Gaza's health ministry says sixteen people were killed in two days.
stories.stand: Hamas confirmed that Samir Abu Younis, head of its Rafah brigade, was killed in an Israeli strike in southern Gaza.
body: An Israeli strike in the Khan Younis area of southern Gaza killed Samir Abu Younis, commander of Hamas's Rafah brigade. Hamas confirmed his death and said he was a senior member of its military wing.
The Israeli military and the Shin Bet security service said they had targeted a senior Hamas military commander. The military said he was directing plans to carry out attacks, ABC News reported.

Al Jazeera reported that the strike hit a tent sheltering displaced people in al-Mawasi, and two others were wounded. Gaza's health ministry says 16 people were killed and 68 injured in the past 48 hours, and at least 1,643 since the October 2025 ceasefire.

stories.head: Iran says it struck US radar in Bahrain; Bahrain reports interceptions
stories.say: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it hit a radar at an American base in Bahrain. Bahrain says it intercepted several Iranian projectiles, and the US has not confirmed any damage.
stories.stand: Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed a strike on a US radar in Bahrain, which said its air defences intercepted several projectiles.
body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it struck a radar system at an American helicopter base in Bahrain. Bahrain said its air defences intercepted several Iranian projectiles.
The US military command had not commented when ABC News reported the claim. Earlier in the week, US Central Command denied a similar Iranian claim to have destroyed a radar in Bahrain.
Al Jazeera described the attacks as retaliatory drone strikes. The claim has not been independently verified.

stories.head: Zelenskyy says US floated giving up Donbas land for Nato entry
stories.say: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says US negotiators asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from part of Donbas in exchange for Nato membership. He says he refused to cede territory.
stories.stand: Ukraine's president says American negotiators raised the idea of ceding parts of Donbas in return for Nato membership, which he says he refused.
body: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US negotiators asked whether Ukraine would give up parts of the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership. He said it was the first time the question had been raised.
Zelenskyy said he had refused to cede territory. He said he would only put any such exchange to Ukrainians if it came with a full package, including security guarantees and reconstruction money.

He told journalists Ukraine needed guarantees similar to Nato's Article 5 as a minimum. The account comes only from Zelenskyy; neither outlet reported a US response. Russia's Vladimir Putin has long called Ukrainian Nato membership a red line.

stories.head: Kushner says he is working to broker Europe-Russia talks on Ukraine
stories.say: US envoy Jared Kushner says he is working to bring Europe and Moscow into direct talks on Ukraine, after leaders agreed to send five European representatives to future negotiations.
stories.stand: The US envoy said he and Steve Witkoff are working on next steps, including direct engagement between Europe and Russia.
body: US envoy Jared Kushner told reporters on Saturday that he is working with Russia, Ukraine and Europe to move peace talks forward, including direct engagement between Europe and Moscow.
He said both sides know compromises will be needed, and that he and Steve Witkoff are working on next steps. Recent talks in Abu Dhabi produced a prisoner exchange but no breakthrough.

Leaders agreed on Friday to send five European representatives to future talks. France's President Emmanuel Macron said Europe must state its post-war goals clearly. The Kremlin signalled openness but criticised the EU for offering few proposals, Al Jazeera reported.

stories.head: South Sudan delays first national election to February
stories.say: South Sudan's first national election has been pushed back again, from the twenty-second of December to the eleventh of February. About ninety percent of people lack state-recognised ID.
stories.stand: The election commission moved the vote from 22 December to 11 February 2027, the latest in a series of delays since 2022.
body: South Sudan's National Elections Commission said the country's first presidential and parliamentary elections will move from 22 December to 11 February 2027.

The commission said the extra time allows registration materials to be distributed and civic education to take place, and stressed the vote is not being abandoned. The election was first expected in 2022.

Voter registration runs until 28 November at more than 3,100 centres. The World Bank estimates about 90% of the 15 million population lack state-recognised ID. Former vice-president Riek Machar has been under house arrest since March.

stories.head: Hungary finds about $20m hidden in forests in Orbán-era graft probe
stories.say: Hungarian investigators have seized about nineteen and a half million dollars, some buried in forests, in a bribery probe into former minister Miklos Sesztak, who denies wrongdoing.
stories.stand: Investigators seized about $19.5m in cash during searches linked to former development minister Miklos Sesztak, who denies wrongdoing.
body: Hungarian investigators seized about $19.5m in hidden cash during searches in Budapest and three other locations, according to the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office.

The money, in forints, euros and dollars, was found in farm buildings, warehouses, a home, a safe and buried in forests. Finance Minister Andras Karman said 12 treasury staff spent eight hours counting it.

The probe targets Miklos Sesztak, development minister from 2014 to 2018, who is suspected of taking bribes. He was detained in September and denies wrongdoing. Viktor Orbán says the investigations aim to force him out of politics.

stories.head: Pope Leo condemns illegal mining and logging on Amazon visit
stories.say: Pope Leo visited Pucallpa in Peru's rainforest on Sunday, criticising the drive behind illegal logging and mining, and condemning sexual violence against Indigenous schoolgirls.
stories.stand: On the penultimate day of his South American tour, the Pope backed Indigenous communities against illegal mining and logging.
body: Pope Leo XIV visited Pucallpa, on the Ucayali river in Peru's rainforest, on Sunday, the penultimate day of a South American tour that began on 6 November.

Speaking to Indigenous representatives and missionaries, he criticised what he called an insatiable thirst for domination behind logging and illegal mining. He cited campaigners' estimate of 57 murders of environmental defenders from 2010 to 2024.
He also condemned the complicity surrounding sexual violence against Indigenous schoolgirls. A local women's council recorded 370 cases from January to July, Euronews reported.

stories.head: Australia and the Philippines sign new defence arrangement
stories.say: Australia and the Philippines have signed a defence arrangement in Manila covering joint patrols, exercises and maritime monitoring. Anthony Albanese said it isn't aimed at any one country.
stories.stand: The deal, signed in Manila on Sunday, updates a 1995 agreement and covers joint patrols, exercises and maritime monitoring.
body: Australia and the Philippines signed a Defence Cooperation Arrangement in Manila on Sunday. Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro and Australia's ambassador Marc Innes-Brown signed it, with Prime Minister Anthony Albanese present.
The deal updates a 1995 agreement. It covers joint patrols, exercises, disaster relief, information sharing, training and maritime monitoring.
Teodoro said it would cut red tape. Albanese said the arrangement is not aimed at any one country. It comes amid tensions in the South China Sea.

stories.head: Francophonie summit opens in Cambodia amid Rwanda-DR Congo row
stories.say: The Francophonie summit has opened in Phnom Penh, with a vote for secretary-general on Monday. DR Congo has threatened to quit if Rwanda's Louise Mushikiwabo wins a third term.
stories.stand: Leaders meet in Phnom Penh as DR Congo threatens to leave the group if Rwanda's Louise Mushikiwabo wins a third term.
body: The 20th Francophonie summit opened in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, on Sunday and runs to Monday. About 20 leaders are expected, including Canada's Mark Carney, Rwanda's Paul Kagame and DR Congo's Felix Tshisekedi.
The dispute centres on Monday's election of a secretary-general. Rwanda's Louise Mushikiwabo, in the post since 2018, is seeking a third term.

DR Congo accuses Rwanda of backing the M23 armed group, which Rwanda denies, and has threatened to leave the organisation if she wins. On Saturday it withdrew its own candidate and backed Dacian Ciolos, Al Jazeera reported.

stories.stand: Energy security, Myanmar, haze and a digital economy deal top the agenda as the Philippines hosts the regional summit.
body: Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations are meeting in Manila this week, with the Philippines hosting.

On Myanmar, UN officials estimate 100,000 people have been killed. Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said a Singapore-Indonesia haze task force should become an ASEAN-wide platform, CNA reported.

stories.say: Iraq's prime minister Ali al-Zaidi has sacked nine senior security and oil officials after a probe into oil smuggling in Jurf al-Nasr, a stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah.
stories.stand: The dismissals followed a probe into illegal refineries in Jurf al-Nasr, a stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah.

The sackings followed an investigation into alleged oil smuggling in Jurf al-Nasr, in Babil province. The area is a stronghold of the Iran-backed armed group Kataib Hezbollah.
The investigation uncovered illegal refineries, and those accused will be referred to the courts, Al Jazeera reported.

stories.head: Fifth Canadian soldier dies after fire at Alberta base
stories.say: A fifth Canadian soldier has died after a grass fire swept across a training range at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in October. Twenty-four remain in hospital.
stories.stand: A wind-driven grass fire swept a training range at CFB Wainwright on 17 October; 24 soldiers remain in hospital.
body: A fifth Canadian soldier has died from injuries suffered when a grass fire swept across a training range at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta on 17 October. The soldier died on Friday in a hospital in Ontario.
About 84 soldiers were training on a grenade launcher range when the wind-driven fire spread. Twenty-four remain in hospital.

Maj Gen Wade Rutland said officials believed the fire was contained and training continued until the wind shifted. Military police are investigating, and a board of inquiry will also examine what happened, CBS News reported.

body: Hundreds of men rallied outside the Swiss parliament in Bern on Saturday to denounce misogyny and violence against women.

Justice Minister Beat Jans said on 2 November that men commit four-fifths of violent crimes, Al Jazeera reported.

stories.head: Nearly 2,200 migrants reach Spain's Canary Islands in two days
stories.say: Nearly two thousand two hundred migrants reached Spain's Canary Islands by boat over two days, most landing on El Hierro, Spain's maritime rescue service says.
stories.stand: Spain's maritime rescue service said most landed on El Hierro, an island of about 12,000 people, days after a migration emergency was declared.
body: Nearly 2,200 migrants reached Spain's Canary Islands by boat over two days, Spain's maritime rescue service said on Sunday, ITV News reported.
The service said it assisted 1,324 people on 14 dinghies, most of whom landed on El Hierro, an island of about 12,000 people. Spain declared a migration emergency on the islands on Tuesday.
The Interior Ministry says over 13,000 of roughly 28,000 sea arrivals in Spain this year landed in the Canaries.

stories.head: Two killed in Leeds after car chased by police hits their vehicle
stories.say: Two people from York have died in Leeds after a BMW being chased by police crashed into their car early on Sunday. Four people from the BMW, three of them teenagers, have been arrested.

body: Two people from York died after a BMW being pursued by police collided with their Volkswagen on Gelderd Road in Leeds at about 12.44am on Sunday, ITV News reported.

West Yorkshire Police said a 39-year-old man from Harrogate was arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and driving over the cannabis limit. Two boys aged 16 and 17 and a 16-year-old girl from the BMW were taken to hospital and also arrested.
The force has referred the crash to the Independent Office for Police Conduct, which has opened an independent investigation.

stories.head: Inquest finds A13 crash deaths avoidable after police went to wrong site
stories.say: An inquest jury has found three deaths after a crash on the A13 in 2024 could have been avoided if Met officers had been given the right location.
stories.stand: A call handler recorded the wrong junction, so officers searched the wrong site after a crash that killed three people.
body: An inquest jury found that three people who died after a crash on the A13 at Wennington junction, Rainham, on 15 July 2024 could have been saved if Metropolitan Police officers had been given the correct location.
Coroner Nina Persaud said a Met call handler failed to record the right location, despite being told it twice. Officers were sent to a different junction in Dagenham.
The Met has since changed its call handler training, including adopting What3Words, ITV News reported.

body: India beat Pakistan by one wicket off the final ball of the Under-19 Asia Cup final near Muscat, Oman, on Saturday, chasing 338 after slipping to 252-8.
After the match, Indian players made aggressive gestures towards Pakistan's players, and the teams skipped the customary handshake, Al Jazeera reported.
Former Pakistan captain Mohammad Yousuf criticised the conduct. No official sanction had been reported.
